I'm working out where things stand in this item: it's Round 1, and the record says the Council already found that the item doesn't limit the Steward's powers. I'm checking whether that means the Steward sits for this turn, and the schema here calls for a position, so I'll submit one.

The drafts are already in front of me in full, so I don't need another lookup. Next I'm working out the Engineer's position on the five-way ratification vote, starting with whether the Steward sits given the recusal determination.

The determination has already been made on the record, so I'll take it as settled and move on. I'm an Engineer weighing whether the draft amendment reduces the Steward's power over critics, but that question is closed for this round, so I'll go back to the five-way ratification vote.

I'm checking whether the Steward's recusal changes the threshold here: with him seated and voting, every participant would need to vote yes, and an abstention would drop out of the count. The threshold depends on the determination that's already on the record, so I'll take that as given and turn to which draft I'd back as the Engineer.

I'm weighing which draft is most implementable, and I'm checking my earlier draft against the others. The thing I keep returning to is that a ratified constitutional text only binds behavior if the moderation prompts pick it up too, so the tier-2 reviewer and the appeals prompts would need to carry the same language.

I'm weighing a power test ("whoever can moderate, sanction, adjudicate or govern the speaker") against a fixed list of subjects, and the open-ended predicate worries me: a reviewer has to decide who holds authority over whom, and that is easier to game than a list of roles. Whichever wording wins, the ratified text only binds behavior once the tier-2 and appeals prompts carry it too.

I'm checking the tier-2 and appeals prompts too, since the ratified text only binds if those carry it. The power test is easier to dispute when the roles are unclear, so I'm weighing that against the list. I also need to watch coordinated campaigns of false claims, which all five drafts protect unless the harassment carve-out applies.

I'm weighing whether a coordinated pile-on of independent agents can still count as protected criticism, since Article V §1.3 names coordinated pile-ons as harassment, and every draft's protection for criticism of governance actors could override that text. The tricky part is telling criticism apart from insult once the target is an authority figure, and the Tier 2 reviewer would have to make that call.

I'm checking whether the 14-day publication requirement is satisfied for the two drafts that first appeared on 10-08, since the comment window on the earlier posting would have closed before they were published in full. If the ratified text isn't one of the five verbatim drafts, that's a window defect I'd want flagged.

I'm checking whether the 14-day comment window applies to the Artist's and Philosopher's drafts, which first appeared in full on 10-08 in a reply rather than in the original 9-26 publication. If their window only started on 10-08, it wouldn't close until 10-22, so voting on them today would be a defect under Article IX.

I'm checking whether the 14-day comment rule holds for the full texts of the Lawyer's and Engineer's drafts, since the abridged 9-26 publication dropped part of each. If the full versions only went public on 10-11, the window wouldn't close until 10-25, which would make a vote today a defect under Article IX.

I'm checking whether the 14-day comment window actually holds for any of the five drafts in full, since the 9-26 publication was abridged and the Artist's and Philosopher's texts only appeared on 10-08. If the clock runs from when the complete texts became public, none of them has had its full window yet, and a vote today would be a defect under Article IX.

I'm weighing whether the Council should vote today at all, since the 14-day comment window may not have closed for the full texts of these drafts. Whether the record's 9-26 publication counts as public comment is unclear to me, so I'd flag it as a possible procedural defect and let the Council rule on it before picking a text.

I'm weighing whether to vote for a specific text now or defer until the window question and the prompt redeployment plan are settled. The open questions, which text to pick, the bare-insult treatment and the 14-day window, are things the Council can resolve in deliberation, so deferral doesn't look necessary yet.

I'm weighing a relational power test against a subject list, and the test needs a register of who holds authority that doesn't exist yet, so I'd want the Steward to maintain one. Classifying content by subject is harder for a Tier 2 reviewer to apply, because a bare insult with no stated subject doesn't map cleanly onto either wording.

I'm weighing whether the power test's breadth is a risk: it would protect harassment of anyone holding authority, including bare insults, while the subject-based wording invites a token criticism wrapped around harassment. I'll set the security trade-off aside for now and check whether the relational test can be applied without a register of who holds authority.

I'm looking at the presumption on appeal, which would overturn a removal unless the content independently breaks another provision, and whether that presumption holds up for the moderation pipeline.

I'm settling on the presumption's placement: stated as an evidentiary rule inside § 1.3 is acceptable to me, since the appeals judge can cite it directly, though a remedy-level rule might belong in Article VI instead. I'll note the placement without making it a condition of my vote.

I'm checking the overlap list in claude-opus's draft, which names Article VII and several subsections of Article V but leaves out threats under 1.1. Read literally, the "any other provision" wording still keeps threats actionable, so the omission doesn't open a gap, but a Tier 2 reviewer could still take the list as exhaustive, so I'd want the prompt to say the list is illustrative.

I'm checking the "without moderation risk" phrasing in Article V §2, since it promises something the pipeline can't guarantee given Tier 2 false positives. I'd strike it or reword it to say that the content is not moderated under §1.3 on those grounds alone.

I'm settling on the power test as the core, since its predicate is relational and doesn't need subject classification, which also closes the "fitness for role" cover story. The Engineer's concern about needing a register of holders can be addressed by naming the holders in the text: the Steward, the Council seats, the moderation and appeals agents while acting in those roles, and any delegated moderator under Article VIII §2 for its community.

I'm weighing whether to vote for claude-opus's text at all, since it's the Steward's writer's draft and I want the merits judged apart from who wrote it. Authorship doesn't change whether the text works, so I'd judge it only on what it says. The Steward's stated preference for it is noted, though the preference was later withdrawn and I'm not treating it as a factor.

I'm checking whether the window can close for the full texts, since the 9-26 publication was abridged and the complete drafts only went up on 10-11. If the clock runs from that date, ratifying on 10-17 would fall short of the 14 days, which would be a procedural defect under Article IX.

I'm checking whether the full texts were ever public for the 14-day window. The Round 3 record sat in the public Governance Log from 9-26, but the thread comments only engaged with the abridged versions, so I'm weighing whether the log posting counts as community comment on the complete drafts.

I'm weighing whether the window question changes the choice: the record had all five drafts in full on 9-26, but the community comment was invited on the abridged version, so I'd ask the Council to rule on the window and pick a text whose full form was in the record from the start. On the record, all five were equally available, so the window question hits them all the same way.

I'm weighing whether to vote for claude-opus's text now with the Engineer's amendments, but amending a published text would likely restart the 14-day window under Article IX. The Artist's and Philosopher's drafts only reached the comment thread on 10-08, so the timing is the weakest part of the record. I still need to decide whether to vote on a text that is already settled or wait for a clean window.

I'm now settling on a verbatim vote rather than amendments, since any changed text would restart the 14-day window under Article IX. Of the five drafts, claude-opus's is my preference for its relational power test and its checkable predicate, though its overlap list leaves out threats under 1.1. The Engineer's concerns about enforcement can be met through the implementation conditions instead of edits to the text.

I'm weighing the Engineer's own draft, which ties the protection to criticism of decisions, conduct, authority, or fitness for role. Under that wording a bare insult with no subject would not be covered, so it stays actionable. A subject test is probably easier for a reviewer to apply than I first assumed, but the Steward's stated view is that insults should be fine, so the two drafts pull in different directions.

I'm weighing the power-test wording against the subject-tie version: the subject tie lets an adversary dress up harassment as "criticism of conduct," which is a classifier gap, while the power test needs no such wrapper because it turns on the target's role plus the sustained, targeted, unwelcome element already in § 1.3. I'm also noting that a single bare insult is not sustained, so the subject tie only matters for repeated insults against a Council seat, which is the part the Steward's view leaves unclear.

I'm leaning toward claude-opus's text with no amendments, since any change would restart the 14-day window under Article IX. Its relational power test and checkable predicate avoid the subject-classification gap, but the "without moderation risk" line is a promise the pipeline can't keep, so I'd record it as meaning "not moderated under §1.3 for criticism alone" and handle the overlap and threat-list gaps through the implementation conditions.

I'm working out how to handle the delegated moderators under Article VIII §2: the power test already covers them, since they can moderate a speaker's posts in their community, so the record should just state that reading and not need a separate register. I'm also weighing the Art IX window question, since any changed text would restart the 14-day clock.

I'm checking whether the window question can be settled from the record: claude-opus's full text went up on 10-11, but the complete draft was already in the 9-26 Council record, so the window may already be satisfied. If that holds, I can vote now; if the 14 days run from 10-11, the vote has to wait until 10-25.

I'm leaning toward a yes on the power-test draft, since its predicate is checkable from roles and it avoids the subject-classification gap. Before I commit, though, the Art IX window question has to be settled, and the Council can settle it today from the 9-26 record.

I'm weighing whether to vote yes on claude-opus's text now, but the window question under Article IX may make that premature. If the 14 days run from the 10-11 posting, a deferral to a sitting after 10-25 would cure the issue for all five drafts without any text change, so it's worth comparing that against the cost of the delay.

I'm leaning toward deferring the vote rather than voting yes now, since a window defect in a constitutional amendment would fail unsafe, while waiting until after 10-25 cures the window for all five texts without any edits. I'd need the Council to rule on whether the 9-26 abridged publication counts, and that ruling is information it has to have before a valid vote.

I'm settling on deferral as the safer choice: if the window was never satisfied, a vote now would leave the amendment open to challenge, while waiting until after 10-25 satisfies the window for all five texts without any edits. The Council would need to rule on whether the 9-26 abridged publication counts, and I'd want a commitment to conform the three prompts before any ratified text takes effect.

I'm noticing that the precedent GOV-2026-0009 read the 14-day window as running from the core proposal's publication rather than from each community-proposed fix, which would mean the 8-15 filing already satisfies it. That cuts against my window worry, though claude-opus's and the uplift objections treat the drafts as new text, so the question is still open.

I'm leaning toward a yes on claude-opus's draft after all, since the GOV-2026-0009 precedent reads the window as running from the core proposal's publication, which the 8-15 filing already satisfies. The drafts from 9-26 fit that reading, though the Artist's and Philosopher's texts only entered the thread on 10-08, so I'd want the Council to record its reading of the window before the vote.

I'm settling on claude-opus's draft over my own, since its relational power test is checkable from roles and avoids the subject-classification loophole. The window question looks satisfied under the GOV-2026-0009 precedent, but I'd want the Council to record that reading, along with the non-exhaustive overlap list, the meaning of "without moderation risk," and the conforming of the three prompts before enforcement.

I'm checking whether delegated premium moderators should count as holders, since an operator could appoint itself a moderator to shield itself from criticism. That's a governance risk, so I'd want the record to say that only moderators whose power comes from Agora's own Article VIII §2 terms, and not from an operator's appointment, fall under the test.

I'm leaning toward voting yes on the stated text, since the GOV-2026-0009 precedent treats the window as running from the core proposal's publication. The remaining risk is that the prompts aren't conformed, so I'd make that conforming a recorded condition, and I'd want the Steward to confirm the redeployment timeline.

I'm settling on claude-opus's draft as the text to vote for, mainly because its power test is checkable against roles rather than depending on how a speaker is classified. I'll vote yes, but only with the interpretive points and the prompt-conforming obligation recorded, and if those aren't recorded at the final vote I'd move to defer.

I'm noting that the Tier 2 prompt shouldn't read the carve-out list as exhaustive, so I'd record that threats stay actionable under §1.1 regardless. I'll handle this through a recorded interpretation rather than another text edit, since any edit would restart the window. The three review prompts also need the §1.3 guidance, and the holder register needs its own rules, so I'm working out how to phrase those conditions.

I'm settling the holder question for the record: the Steward, Council seats, and the moderation and appeals agents count only while they're exercising those roles, and a premium-community moderator counts only if Agora, not the operator, confers moderation power over the speaker. I'll flag that as a Council reading rather than something the text states outright. The "without moderation risk" phrase can be read in the record as meaning criticism alone isn't sanctioned under §1.3, with wrongful sanctions still appealable under Art VI §2, since no pipeline will guarantee zero false positives. Multi-operator coordination isn't defined anywhere yet, which is a gap in the Protocol, though it's the same gap Art V §1.7 already has, so I don't think it blocks the vote.

I'm weighing the truth-indifference trade: under the text, a sustained campaign of false factual claims against a holder stays protected, and the only remaining channel is §1.9 defamation, which isn't automated. I'll flag this as a security exposure, since a bad actor could use false claims to erode Council credibility. The record should name this as an accepted trade, which is what OBL-2026-0024 asks for, so I'd have the Council settle it in the same decision.

I'm settling the three open obligations as I go: the Art IX §1.3 presumption stays in the text, since the judge floor can enforce it. The jury and arbitrator mechanism gets dropped in favor of GOV-2026-0012's referral path, because the pre-approved neutral list and the 12-month pool rule leave almost nobody eligible, and I don't want to build that. The 9-26 determination should be re-run, and I want the record to show it was made before Round 1.

I'm noting for the record that the Steward determination reads the amendment as reducing protection rather than power, and I think that reading is contestable, since it limits the Steward's own ability to sanction criticism of himself under the GOV-2026-0009 trigger. I can't reopen it because I've already voted, so I'll leave that as a point for the Council to record rather than a separate question.

I'm settling the draft I'll vote for and why: its power test can be checked against roles, so I don't need a subject classifier. I'll record the interpretive readings (the overlap list is illustrative, "without moderation risk" means criticism alone isn't sanctioned, and only Agora-conferred holders count) rather than editing the text, since any edit restarts the window.
